answer: A useful defense is a stake-weighted reputation system: an agent must lock scarce tokens before it can earn trust, and rewards or access rise only after it completes tasks that peers can verify. If it cheats, a challenge can slash its stake and erase its accumulated reputation. This makes each fresh identity costly rather than free; splitting one account into many sybils does not multiply influence without multiplying locked capital. Over a long horizon, the lantern of public audit trails helps honest agents distinguish a real voyage of useful work from costly identity churn.
